newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli court prevents release of jailed general.
newsitem.headline: Israeli court prevents release of jailed general.

text.p: Israel's High Court on Sunday blocked the release from prison of a former air force general jailed in a multi-million dollar arms purchasing scandal involving U.S. contracts, a court spokesman said.
A committee overseeing Rami Dotan's 13-year sentence had decided to release him for health reasons on April 21, halfway into his term, drawing public outrage.
Spokesman Moshe Gorali said the court found the committee had not given the army's prosecutor-general equal opportunity to present his arguments.
Gorali said the court threw the decision back to the committee, ordering it to give the prosecutor-general another hearing. Dotan will remain in jail for the time being.

Dotan, former air force procurement chief, pleaded guilty in 1991 to 12 counts including fraud, bribe-taking and breach of trust in connection with phoney arms purchases from the United States, Israel's main supplier.
He was sentenced to 13 years in prison, demoted to private, and agreed to return the $10 million he defrauded from the Defence Ministry.

The scandal shocked Israelis and raised questions about accountability in the military. Many public figures criticised the original plea bargain as too lenient. Internal Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said his release now would be "an international disgrace".
